Sure! Here is the information I provided about command hallucinations and olfactory phantosmia (olfactory hallucinations) and parosmia (olfactory illusions):

Command hallucinations are voices that one hears and they tell the listener what to do. These can range from simple directives like "Stand up" or "Shut the door" to more threatening commands. Command hallucinations are often associated with schizophrenia. Some helpful questions that can assist one in determining if they may have this includes: "What are the voices telling you to do?", "When did your voices first start telling you to do things?", "Do you recognize the person who is telling you to harm yourself (or others)?", "Do you think you can resist doing what the voices are telling you to do?"

Olfactory Phantosmia (olfactory hallucinations), smelling an odor that is not actually there, and parosmia (olfactory illusions), inhaling a real odor but perceiving it as different scent than remembered, are distortions to the sense of smell (olfactory system). In most cases, these are not caused by anything serious and will usually go away on their own in time. It can result from a range of conditions such as nasal infections, nasal polyps, dental problems, migraines, head injuries, seizures, strokes, or brain tumors. Environmental exposures can sometimes cause it as well, such as smoking, exposure to certain chemicals, or changes in the weather. If you are experiencing persistent olfactory hallucinations or illusions, it is important to consult with a healthcare professional to determine the underlying cause and appropriate treatment.
